hero.title: See what is live, what is in development, and what each project is proving.
hero.lede: These examples show LDW's own website, product-development work, and internal service-enabling infrastructure without presenting unfinished systems as completed customer results.

projects.name: Lowcountry Digital Works website
projects.description: A lightweight, accessibility-tested Astro website with repository-controlled content, local brand assets, and Cloudflare edge delivery.
projects.purpose: Prove that a small business site can be fast, maintainable, visually disciplined, and owned through ordinary source control without a CMS or tracking stack.
evidence: Astro static output with Cloudflare Workers Static Assets
Playwright and axe browser/accessibility regression coverage
Documented deployment, rollback, and ownership boundaries
boundaries: No CMS, database, analytics, customer account system, or public contact-form processor.
Production changes remain protected by PR review and explicit launch gates.
projects.imageAlt: Lowcountry Digital Works public website homepage before the 0.7.0 visual refresh

projects.name: Document Control
projects.description: An LDW-developed workflow system exploring structured document lifecycle, review, accountability, audit history, search, export, and administrative configuration.
projects.purpose: Explore how exact-version document workflows can be made more understandable and auditable while keeping product development portable and repository controlled.
boundaries: Active development is not presented as a completed customer deployment.
Commercial validation remains service-first and separately governed.

projects.name: Secure Exchange
projects.description: A provider-neutral product direction for protected external intake and outbound delivery, queue-based staff workflows, retention, and sanitized audit history.
projects.purpose: Test a customer-owned isolated delivery model for sensitive workflow needs while preserving clear provider, retention, and accountability boundaries.
evidence: External intake and outbound delivery workflow design
Individual workforce accountability and queue routing
Provider-neutral core with customer-owned deployment direction
boundaries: Production customer infrastructure is not represented as deployed here.
Regulated-data use remains subject to customer-specific security, legal, and platform gates.

projects.name: G.A.S. Engine
projects.description: LDW-operated internal evidence and measurement infrastructure used to normalize and retain website-quality observations for managed-service learning.
projects.purpose: Help LDW compare website evidence over time without turning a one-time scan score into a customer-facing product claim.
evidence: Longitudinal normalized evidence within its accepted scope
Designed to support, not replace, authoritative evidence sources
boundaries: Not customer SaaS, not a self-service SEO platform, and not a standalone commercial product.
Managed Search + AI Visibility remains separately gated under its own validation track.

principle.title: The stack should serve the work, not become the work.
principle.body: A static website, an automation, a configured SaaS workflow, or a focused custom application can all be the right answer in different situations. The goal is the smallest maintainable system that meets the real requirement.
